Jorge Assis, PhD // Nord University, Norway // biodiversityDS, Centre of Marine Sciences, Portugal

The diversity of algorithms

biodiversityDS .

Species Distribution Models (SDMs) are a powerful tool to assess the potential distribution of species in response to environmental changes. The diversity of algorithms and ensembles is a key aspect, as it allows for the integration of different approaches to improve predictions.

# read occurrence records (presences) and transform to spatial object
presences <- read.table("../Data/Text delimited/species_presence_records.csv", sep = ";", header = TRUE)
presences <- vect(presences, geom = c("Lon", "Lat"))
S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# download layers for present conditions
variables <- list(var1 = c("thetao", "mean", "depthmean"), var2 = c("o2", "mean", "depthmean"),
    var3 = c("phyc", "mean", "depthmean"))
environmentalLayers <- download_multiple_layers(variables = variables, experiment = c("baseline"),
    decade = c(2010))
# plot layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# develop a study region layer
myStudyRegion <- studyRegion(rasterLayers=environmentalLayers, # SpatRaster of layers
                             presences=presences, # presence records
                             distanceThreshold=200000, # distance from records in meters
                             bathymetryLayer = "../Data/Raster data/Bathymetry.tif", # bathymetry layer
                             depthPref=c(-15,-300)) # known vertical distribution
# inspect the study region layer
plot(myStudyRegion, main="Study region", col="#979797", axes=TRUE)

S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# crop and mask the environmental layers to the study region
environmentalLayers <- crop(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
environmentalLayers <- mask(environmentalLayers, myStudyRegion)
# plot the masked environmental layers
plot(environmentalLayers, axes = TRUE)

S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# generate pseudo-absences and combine presences and absences into a unique object
absences <- pseudoAbsences(rasterLayers = environmentalLayers, presences = presences, n = 1000)
presences$PA <- 1
absences$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(absences, presences)
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, envConditions = environmentalLayers, method = "blocks",
    kFolds = 6)
## Warning ::  665  records were removed because they have missing values in the environmental data
S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .

Generalised linear models

# fit a brt model to the dataset
modelGLM <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "glm")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
predictionGLM <- predictModel(model = modelGLM, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(predictionGLM$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# keep model performance in a object
modelPerformanceGLM <- modelGLM$performance[modelGLM$performance$dataset == "test", ]
# inspect model performance
modelPerformanceGLM

Boosted regression trees

# fit a brt model to the dataset
hyperparametersList <- list(learning.rate = c(0.1, 0.01, 0.001), interaction.depth = c(2, 3,
    4), n.trees = seq(100, 1000, by = 100))
modelBRT <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "brt", hyperparameters = hyperparametersList)
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
predictionBRT <- predictModel(model = modelBRT, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(predictionBRT$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

Extreme gradient boosting

# fit a xgboost model to the dataset
hyperparametersList <- list(shrinkage = c(0.1, 0.01, 0.001), depth = c(2, 3, 4), rounds = c(10,
    50, 100), gamma = c(0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1))
modelXGBOOST <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "xgboost", hyperparameters = hyperparametersList)
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
predictionXGBOOST <- predictModel(model = modelXGBOOST, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(predictionXGBOOST$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

Maximum entropy (MaxEnt)

# generate pseudo-absences and combine presences and absences into a unique object
background <- backgroundInformation(rasterLayers = environmentalLayers, n = 10000)
presences$PA <- 1
background$PA <- 0
records <- rbind(background, presences)
# extract environmental values and make an object with all information to model
modelData <- generateModelData(records, envConditions = environmentalLayers, method = "blocks",
    kFolds = 6)
## Warning ::  665  records were removed because they have missing values in the environmental data
S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# fit a maxent model to the dataset
hyperparametersList <- list(betamultiplier = c(0.5, 1, 5, 10, 25), feature = c("ht", "lp", "lq",
    "tc", "th", "h", "l", "q", "p", "t"))
modelMaxent <- trainModel(modelData, algorithm = "maxent")
# predict the distribution with the model over a raster stack
predictionMaxent <- predictModel(model = modelMaxent, newData = environmentalLayers)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(predictionMaxent$rasterLayer, main = "Predicted species distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))

S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .

Ensembling different models

To reduce uncertainty in the predictions, we can ensemble different models (e.g. averaging predictions).

# combining the predictions of the three models
prediction <- c(predictionGLM$rasterLayer, predictionBRT$rasterLayer, predictionXGBOOST$rasterLayer,
    predictionMaxent$rasterLayer)
# determine the average prediction and the uncertainty
ensemble <- app(prediction, fun = mean)
uncertainty <- app(prediction, fun = sd)
# map the predicted distribution
plot(ensemble, main = "Ensembled predicted distribution", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))
S8 // The diversity of algorithms and ensembles

biodiversityDS .
# map the uncertainty of the predictions
plot(uncertainty, main = "Algorithm uncertainty", col = rev(topo.colors(100)))
